title: Baseball History in Data
text:
This site explores the history of Major League Baseball since 1871 using the Lahman Baseball Database, focusing on how power hitting has evolved across more than a century and a half of play. Looking at league-wide totals first reveals sharp, misleading drops during players’ strikes and the COVID-shortened 2020 season—but once we measure home runs per game, those shortened seasons sit right on the historical curve, highlighting a dramatic rise from the dead-ball era to the modern long-ball game.
Zooming in from league trends to individual hitters tells a matching story: more than half of MLB’s top 15 all-time career home-run leaders played during the 1994–2009 steroid era, topped by Barry Bonds and his extraordinary late-career surge to 73 home runs in 2001.
